cards.title: Memory
cards.purpose: Keep useful information across conversations. Inspect tier instructions below. On supported agents, Enable Memory Lite offers a separate preview and confirmed Save.
requirements: A writable memory root; Journal and BuJo also need local embeddings.
cards.usage: Lite stays local. Journal adds embeddings. BuJo also uses extraction-model tokens.
steps: In the agent folder, back up mono-agent.config.json. Merge only the shown fields; preserve unrelated settings, existing allowlists and deny rules. Replace every example placeholder before use. These manual steps do not apply changes. Only agents advertising console Enable support offer typed Memory Lite and cron-control actions.

Run mono-agent validate. Resolve waiting/error findings before starting. Restart a managed agent with mono-agent restart; for foreground use stop/start in its terminal. Validation is readiness evidence, not proof of message delivery.

variants.title: Journal (semantic recall)
variants.purpose: Semantic recall via local Ollama or LM Studio embeddings.
requirements: A fresh memory root, SQLite, and a running Ollama or LM Studio embedding model with matching dimension.
variants.usage: Local embedding compute and disk usage; rebuild embeds stored content. Embedding/model liveness is not probed here; run mono-agent validate in the owner terminal.
steps: In the agent folder, back up mono-agent.config.json. Merge only the shown fields; preserve unrelated settings, existing allowlists and deny rules. Replace every example placeholder before use. These manual steps do not apply changes. Only agents advertising console Enable support offer typed Memory Lite and cron-control actions.
Use this recipe only for a fresh root. Stop the agent before preparing memory: mono-agent stop
Set the actual embedding model, endpoint and dimension; for BuJo set the extraction model too.
Initialize generation metadata from the agent folder: mono-agent memory rebuild
Do not change an existing root tier or rebuild/migrate existing data from these instructions; use the memory administration guide.

Run mono-agent validate. Resolve waiting/error findings before starting. Restart a managed agent with mono-agent restart; for foreground use stop/start in its terminal. Validation is readiness evidence, not proof of message delivery.

cards.title: Scheduled jobs (cron)
cards.purpose: Run the agent on a schedule; scaffolds cron/digest.md.
requirements: At least one enabled job markdown file in cron/. Review its schedule before starting.
cards.usage: Every scheduled run may consume model tokens, tools and notification usage.
steps: In the agent folder, back up mono-agent.config.json. Merge only the shown fields; preserve unrelated settings, existing allowlists and deny rules. Replace every example placeholder before use. These manual steps do not apply changes. Only agents advertising console Enable support offer typed Memory Lite and cron-control actions.
Create cron/digest.md with the following contents:

---
expression: "0 8 * * *"
conversationId: cron-digest
notify: true
---

Produce a concise digest of anything noteworthy since the last run.
Your final reply is delivered to the user verbatim as the notification — write it as the finished message, with no preface. If nothing is noteworthy, call FinishSilently({}) alone without narration. If that tool is unavailable, reply with exactly NOTHING_TO_REPORT.

Run mono-agent validate. Resolve waiting/error findings before starting. Restart a managed agent with mono-agent restart; for foreground use stop/start in its terminal. Validation is readiness evidence, not proof of message delivery.

cards.title: MCP / tools
cards.purpose: Let the agent use local tools and owner-prepared MCP servers.
requirements: An explicit built-in tool policy and, for external MCP, an existing validated MCP JSON file. External MCP tools bypass built-in allow/deny rules.
cards.usage: Tool use can add model turns, subprocesses and third-party service costs. External MCP server connectivity is never probed by validation. Computer-use and provider/browser liveness are not probed here; run mono-agent validate in the owner terminal.
steps: Back up mono-agent.config.json; preserve existing deny rules. Merge only the tool names you intend to allow.
{ "tools": { "allowedTools": ["Read", "Glob", "Grep"], "mcpConfigPath": "./mcp.json" } }
Prepare and review mcp.json in the owner terminal before referencing it. Do not run untrusted server commands. Omit mcpConfigPath if you only want built-in tools.
For optional desktop control, prepare cua-driver and tools.computerUse in the owner terminal; follow https://docs.mono-agent.dev/tools/computer-use/ for installation, permissions and manual checks.
Run mono-agent validate, then mono-agent restart for a managed agent or stop/start in the foreground terminal.

cards.title: Built-in tracing
cards.purpose: Already enabled: the app records local run evidence for diagnostics and discovery.
requirements: No extra exporter or service is required.
cards.usage: Local disk usage; no separate model calls. External trace exporters are not supported.
steps: No enable step is needed. Use mono-agent runs to inspect local run evidence. Phoenix/OTLP exporters were removed and cannot be enabled.
